label: Stiefel manifolds
notes: This short chapter, printed pages 130 to 134, introduces the Stiefel manifold of orthonormal frames. We frame it as a curved sample space sitting inside Euclidean matrix space, which is exactly the setup the book exploits for extrinsic statistical inference on frame and shape data.

label: Definition of V_k,m
notes: The Stiefel manifold is the set of m-by-k matrices whose columns form an orthonormal k-frame, captured by the single matrix equation X-transpose-X equals the identity. Each constraint removes degrees of freedom, and counting them gives the manifold dimension we derive next.

label: Dimension count
notes: We count constraints in the symmetric equation X-transpose-X equals identity. The k diagonal unit-norm conditions plus the k-choose-two off-diagonal orthogonality conditions subtract from the km free entries, yielding dimension km minus k times k plus one over two.

label: Special cases
notes: Two special cases anchor intuition. A single orthonormal vector is just a point on the unit sphere, so V one m equals S to the m minus one. A full frame of m vectors is an orthogonal matrix, so V m m equals the orthogonal group O of m.

label: Orthonormal 2-frame in R^3
notes: Here we picture a point of V two three: two perpendicular unit vectors in three-space. Their span is a plane, but the frame remembers the actual ordered pair of axes, not just the plane. This distinction is what makes the frame, not the subspace, the data object.

label: Equivariant embedding
notes: The Stiefel manifold inherits the Euclidean inner product of matrix space, the Frobenius inner product. Left multiplication by an orthogonal matrix preserves the constraint and the metric, so the embedding is equivariant, which is precisely the property extrinsic analysis needs.

label: Extrinsic mean idea
notes: For extrinsic analysis we average frames in the ambient matrix space, then project the Euclidean average back onto the manifold. The average of orthonormal frames is generally not orthonormal, so a well-defined projection map to the nearest frame is the heart of the construction.

label: Polar projection via SVD
notes: The nearest orthonormal frame to a generic matrix is found by polar decomposition. Writing the average as U-Sigma-V-transpose, the projection keeps the rotational factor U-V-transpose and discards the singular values, giving the unique closest point in Frobenius distance when the matrix has full rank.

label: Residual diagnostics
notes: After projecting we check the residual: how far X-transpose-X sits from the identity tells us the orthogonality error, and the singular values of the average measure how concentrated the frame sample is. These diagnostics certify that the estimator stayed on the manifold.

label: Link to shape spaces
notes: Stiefel manifolds connect to shape statistics through pre-shapes and the reflection-shape Gram construction. Scaled orthonormal frames represent centered configurations, and quotienting by rotation yields shape; the Gram matrix X-transpose-X gives reflection-invariant shape coordinates used later in the book.

label: Summary
notes: To summarize: the Stiefel manifold of orthonormal frames has dimension km minus k k plus one over two, specializes to spheres and orthogonal groups, embeds equivariantly in matrix space, and supports an extrinsic mean computed by polar projection. These tools feed directly into shape and directional inference.
